analysis: Examined the changes in this batch. (1) EngineV2Bridge+StopSequence.swift (head lines 14-32): the matched-stop-sequence reporter now takes an optional CBv2StopStringScope and replays StopHoldback over the decoded text, so the reported stop matches the scoped engine behavior (GPT-OSS Harmony final-channel). The unscoped path is unchanged. This only affects which stop string is reported to the client from the model's own output. I found no new disclosure or authorization surface. The scoped path returns nil if the scan did not stop, which is a correctness fallback, not a security downgrade. (2) EngineV2Bridge+Submission.swift (head lines 249-250): `stopStringScope` is forwarded to the CBv2Request. `stopStringScope` is a bridge property; its definition is not in the supplied evidence, and neither are `StopHoldback` or `CBv2StopStringScope`. Both live in submodule or unchanged code. I assume these are non-nil only for trusted model policy and not client-controlled. (3) docs/architecture/inference.md: documentation only, covering the MiMo, Flint and stop-scope descriptions. No control changes. It states that restoring MiMo tool schemas grants no tool, media or memory-admission bypass. This is a claim that the submodule diff cannot confirm here. (4) Submodule pointer bumps, libs/mlx, libs/mlx-swift and libs/mlx-swift-lm: only commit hashes are visible, and their contents are not supplied. They can affect TB-007 (inference engine), T-041 (prefix-cache and KV SSD), T-028 and MiMo or Flint decode and memory admission. I have not reviewed them. They need separate review of the submodule diffs, especially anything touching the encrypted KV cache, GlobalKVCacheBudget or stop-string handling. No threat-model assumption is invalidated by the visible Swift or doc changes, so I am reporting no findings. needs_deeper_review is true only because of the unreviewed submodule content.
